svg.text: CONTAINER HOUSE
5 × 40 ft High Cube · 2 bedrooms · ≈148 m² gross
Freestanding, rural plot · Mediterranean climate
Prepared for David Budzik
GENERAL NOTES
All dimensions in metres unless noted; levels from ±0.00 = finished ground. Container sizes are nominal 40
ft HC (12.19 × 2.44 × 2.90 m); verify against the purchased units. All steel (posts, lintels, seam beams,
void trimmers) and foundations to structural engineer's design. Do not scale. Concept stage — for design
coordination and the Blender model only.

DESIGN DECISIONS (ADR SUMMARY)
Places where drawing the brief exposed a conflict. Full records in ADR.md. Status: Accepted by David Budzik, 28 Oct 2026.
ADR-001 Upper-floor circulation
CONTEXT
The brief orders the upper floor as main bedroom (0–4.2) | ensuite +
walk-in (4.2–6.4) | bath (5.6–7.6) | landing (6.4+). Read literally, the
main bedroom has no door to the landing: every route passes through a wet
room.
DECISION
Run a 0.80 m hall from the landing westward to the main bedroom between
the ensuite (north) and the walk-in + bath (south). Ensuite 5.0→4.1 m²,
walk-in 3.0→2.1 m², bath 4.5→3.6 m².
OPTIONS NOT TAKEN
Rejected: B) swap bedrooms so the main is at the east end — loses the west
view glass the brief wants for the main bedroom. C) reach the main bedroom
through the walk-in — the dressing room becomes the corridor, ensuite
still cut off.
ADR-002 Stair on north, WC internal
CONTEXT
The brief puts the stair in C1's north strip and the WC + laundry in C1's
south strip beside it, but also gives the WC a slot window. A south-strip
WC has no outside wall.
DECISION
Keep the stair on the north wall (the W06 slots light the flight). The WC
is internal: continuous mechanical extract, high borrowed light over the
door. The upper wet rooms sit above the kitchen, so the soil stack drops
in the tall-unit / under-stair zone at x ≈ 7.5.
OPTIONS NOT TAKEN
Rejected: swap stair and WC strips — the stair would sit against the open
hall and lose the slot windows, and the WC would face the north service
side next to the heat-pump units.
ADR-003 D02 red doors: inside face only
CONTEXT
The original red doors are the feature wall at the foot of the stair, but
they are also the external end wall of C1. Insulating on the inside hides
them; leaving them bare makes a 7 m² uninsulated steel wall.
DECISION
Keep the doors bare inside and insulate outside: ≈80 mm insulation and a
charcoal corrugated over-cladding panel on the east face of C1. The east
facade reads as continuous charcoal; the red is an interior moment.
OPTIONS NOT TAKEN
Rejected: bare doors both sides (thermal bridge and condensation in a
heated stair void). Also noted: W09 east glazing to C3 is added because
the brief asks for glass on both short ends but schedules none on the
east.
ASSUMPTIONS IN THESE DRAWINGS
· Levels: piers 400 mm, GF FFL +0.55, UF FFL +3.45 (floor-to-floor 2.90 = one container), roof top +6.50.
· Wall build-up 150 mm (steel + 50–80 closed-cell foam + stud + board); clear height ≈2.45 m both floors.
· Plot is illustrative (28 × 32 m). Orientation: long glazed facade due south.
· New steel shown as intent only — sizes, connections and pier layout are for the structural engineer.
· Optional cantilever (upper block 1.2–2.4 m past the west end) not drawn; base design only.
OPEN QUESTIONS (from the brief, still open)
☐ Which plot: size, slope, view direction, zoning (agricultural or residential)?
☐ Budget ceiling — does the ≈₪2M reference include land? Get a container-builder quote against this set.
☐ Bedroom 2: guest, kids' room or studio / office?
☐ Base design or cantilevered upper floor?
☐ Israeli permit: a mamad (safe room) is normally required for a new home — the brief mentions a
'safe-room block' collection but places none. Needs a decision before permit drawings.
NEXT STEPS

1) ADR-001…003 accepted. 2) Survey + soil report for the chosen plot. 3) Structural engineer sizes the seam beams, posts, lintels and piers. 4) Build the Blender massing from these levels (object names = W/D codes). 5) Hero
render, shot 10 (aerial at dusk). 6) Resolve mamad position, then develop toward permit drawings.
